page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at 3.3 GHz. The processor architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by hardware AES acceleration. System memory totals 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, includes zero bundled local storage, and features no accelerator GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded and memory-subsystem efficiency. In Geekbench, the instance achieves a top-tier single-core score of 2337.0 alongside high text-processing throughput (3052.0). Data decompression and compression routines excel, with single-threaded gzip hitting 36.5 GB/sec and bzip3 reaching 17.09 GB/sec, both placing in the top decile. PassMark memory testing also registers in the top 10% at 3745.62 points. Conversely, broader multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng (8018.98) and Geekbench multi-core (7556.0) perform within the median range. Standard PassMark CPU tests show weak relative output, particularly in extended instruction and synthetic encryption suites, reflecting ARMv9 instruction set differences against x86-oriented tests.

The absence of internal NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached block storage for persistent data, which balances operational flexibility against I/O overhead. Resource density and low architectural overhead deliver solid operational cost efficiency for general compute jobs that do not demand specialized vector extensions or massive parallel thread counts. While smaller language models run adequately (234.42 tokens/sec generation on 135M models), prompt processing on 7B models falls into the bottom tier at 11.27 tokens/sec.

The m9g.xlarge is well aligned for mid-tier application workloads, including microservices, web serving (demonstrating 14.82 GB/sec static throughput), in-memory caching platforms such as Redis (processing 12.65 million SET operations/sec), build environments, and containerized business software.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores clocked at 3.3 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance operates without multithreading, providing one dedicated physical thread per vCPU. It includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, utilizing a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark profiles demonstrate top-tier single-core Geekbench performance (2337.0), leading memory benchmark results, and high single-threaded compression throughput, though multi-threaded synthetic integer and PassMark CPU scores remain closer to fleet averages. The instance offers strong cost efficiency for ARM-compatible workloads requiring predictable single-thread execution, moderate memory bandwidth, and stable application scaling. Its hardware profile is well suited for containerized microservices, Redis caching nodes, standard web servers, and continuous integration pipelines.
